title: Family wants answers in SIU case
article: When Susana Chavvaria got into a dispute with her husband at their west-end apartment two weeks ago, she called the cops for help.
Rodrigo Almonacid Gonzalez, 43, was wheeled out of their Dora Ave. highrise on a stretcher 90 minutes later and by the next day, Chavvaria was a widow with two fatherless kids.
"His wife feels so guilty because she called the police," Yasmin Almonacid said Thursday of her sister-in-law. "She never imagined my brother would end up dead."
The family's lawyer, Davin Charney, said the couple had a "small" dispute prior to Chavvaria calling 911, but he wouldn't elaborate.
He said six Toronto Police officers arrived at the building near Bloor St. W. and Lansdowne Ave. shortly after midnight on Nov. 6.
"The officers wouldn't allow Almonacid Gonzales' wife or his mother to enter the apartment," Charney said. "We understand, but can't say for certain, he shut himself in the bathroom."
For reasons he says he still can't comprehend, nine emergency task force officers responded to the scene.
"We don't believe he represented a threat to himself or anybody else at that point," Charney said.
He claims Almonacid Gonzalez wasn't drunk or on drugs, nor did he have mental-health issues or access to weapons.

It's believed cops bashed in the door and Tasered Almonacid Gonzalez twice - one of the few details mentioned by Ontario's Special Investigations Unit when it revealed Wednesday it's probing the death.
SIU spokesman Jason Gennaro said police notified the unit immediately.
Police are prohibited by law from commenting on an ongoing SIU investigation into their conduct.
So it's unclear what else was done to try to subdue Almonacid Gonzalez.
But in photos the family shot later, the bathroom looked like a tornado swept through.
Almonacid Gonzalez' face was badly swollen and bruised when he died Nov. 7.
"His injuries were consistent with a brutal beating," Charney said. "And he was never able to speak again."
"I don't understand why they didn't try to de-escalate the situation."
Yasmin Almonacid said her brother, who was only about 5-foot-3 and 145 lbs., leaves behind two sons, 12 and 20.
The younger boy isn't doing well, she said, adding he's upset his dad won't be around for his birthday Saturday.
His father's funeral will be held the next day.
Surveillance video from a west-end highrise shows Toronto Police arriving just after midnight on Nov. 6. Around 1:30 a.m., paramedics are seen rolling Rodrigo Almonacid Gonzalez out on a stretcher.
The 43-year-old man's family believes what happened during those 90 minutes resulted in his death the next day in hospital.
12:01 a.m.: A single officer walks upstairs to the apartment where Almonacid Gonzalez is believed to be holed up in a bathroom.
12:07 a.m.: Two more cops are met by Almonacid Gonzalez's mom in the lobby and the trio calmly ride the elevator up to the apartment.
12:19 a.m.: Almonacid Gonzalez's wife greets another three cops in the lobby and they all calmly head up in the elevator.
12:24 a.m.: Almonacid Gonzalez's wife and mother, after allegedly being told to stay out of the apartment, ride the elevator back down to the lobby with two officers.
12:28 a.m.: Toronto EMS arrives and two paramedics bring a stretcher into the lobby.
12:58 a.m.: Seven emergency task force officers carrying riot shields, a battering ram, saw and other tools arrive and take the stairs up to the apartment.
12:59 a.m.: Two more ETF officers arrive and head up to the apartment.
1:32 a.m.: Two paramedics wheel Almonacid Gonzalez into an elevator on a stretcher and are joined by one uniform cop and one ETF officer.
1:34 a.m.: Strapped to the stretcher, Almonacid Gonzalez is wheeled out through the lobby to an ambulance as his head thrashes back and forth.
1:35 a.m.: ETF officers walk down the stairs to the lobby and leave the building.
Almonacid Gonzalez was taken to St. Joseph's Health Centre. Hours later, he was moved to the intensive care unit, where he died the next day.
